request: What are the estimated budget costs of clean energy tax credits?

reply.reply:
At enactment, JCT estimated that the Inflation Reduction Act’s energy tax credits and deductions together would increase deficits by $271 billion over FY2022–FY2031. This is the broadest verified estimate found, but it is not a credits-only estimate. (CRS R46865, PDF p. 3; report dated February 26, 2024.)

The estimate is an enactment-era figure, not a later revision. The brief explains the scope and caveats.
reply.reasoning: The verified estimate combines energy tax credits and deductions, so it answers the question only partially; no verified estimate isolates clean-energy tax credits alone.
